existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: Measure has material R4-to-R6 breaks: root interpretation metadata moved to groups, several documentation/categorization fields were removed or restructured, and R6 allows population/stratifier definitions that R4 cannot model.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Use group-aware transforms, preserve removed documentation deliberately, update evaluators for optional criteria and new alternatives, and refresh terminology caches/enums.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural deltas from the two StructureDefinitions. It is lower for terminology equivalence and rationale because external expansions and official diffs were unavailable.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
Measure keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 4 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 1 potential hard break(s), 4 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 16 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 2, which creates neutral stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 100/100, producing migration shape `major-model-remodel`, major migration `Partial`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

6 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

10 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Use less-breaking designs where they do not preserve obsolete or conflicting models indefinitely.
